text:
maria (AE): Hey team — customer wants a Private deployment + on-prem proxy POC. They're asking: can we guarantee a stable egress IP for firewall allowlist, what ports/protocols to open, and how that affects pricing for POC vs prod? Need quick answers for their security questionnaire.

chris (SE): Short answers: yes, we can provide stable egress IPs if they proxy egress through a NAT/egress EIP from their network or via our managed egress in Dedicated. PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is recommended for control-plane+API; traffic egress to internet still needs a NAT/proxy on their side or our egress appliance.

olivia (NetOps): For the typical on-prem -> Privatedeploy flow we ask customers to allow outbound to our interface endpoint IPs and (for proxy) to the egress IP. Minimal firewall snippet: 

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood endpoints
ALLOW tcp 443 -> 52.11.x.x/32  # interface endpoint
ALLOW tcp 443 -> <egress-eip>  # optional managed egress
# DNS
ALLOW udp 53 -> 8.8.8.8
```

olivia (NetOps): If they terminate TLS inspection, SNI gets rewritten and client certs may break. Prefer allowlist by IP + mTLS for control-plane. Also note: preserving client source IP across PrivateLink isn't possible — requests from our infra will show provider IP unless they use passthrough proxy.

adam (CISO): We need specifics for the questionnaire: is traffic encrypted in transit end-to-end? Where are keys stored? Can you confirm we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments?

chris (SE): TL;DR: yes encrypted (TLS 1.2/1.3). For Private deployments we offer customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS/HSM) for at-rest model and token encryption. Add this line to the security doc: "All inter-service traffic is TLS 1.3; control-plane keys can be bound to customer KMS in Private mode."

sales-eng: On pricing: POC pricing commonly uses a short-term Dedicated burst or trial credits. Two levers affect cost: egress data transfer (per-GB) and reserved instance/GPU-hours for Dedicated. Quick calc: 

- GPU hourly * hours + egress GB * $0.12 = ballpark.

maria (AE): Can you put together an itemized checklist I can send to the customer (ports, sample SGs, proof points for KMS + egress IP approach)? Also they asked about a fallback to hosted API if capacity drops — any auto-fallback options?

chris (SE): Checklist: 
- PrivateLink interface endpoints (control plane)
- Egress strategy: customer-managed NAT with static IP OR Redwood managed egress (dedicated eip)
- Firewall rules: outbound 443 to endpoints + DNS
- TLS/mTLS expectation, KMS integration confirmed
- Test plan: smoke requests + auth + sample prompt latency

Auto-fallback: we support policy-based routing — for Dedicated we can configure automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted model variant (with lower SLA) if capacity constraints are hit. That requires routing policy and agreed QoS in the POC.

olivia (NetOps): Test plan snippet for them to run during POC: 
```
# verify reachability
curl -v https://<interface-endpoint>/healthz --resolve '<interface-endpoint>:443:52.11.x.x'
# send sample inference
curl -X POST https://<endpoint>/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
```

maria (AE): Perfect. I'll fold this into the security questionnaire answers and the preflight checklist. Can someone paste the exact IP ranges for the interface endpoints and the managed egress EIP(s) we can offer for the POC?

chris (SE): I'll DM the exact /32 addresses (they rotate per-region) and include the fallback routing config. Expect the DM in ~30m.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: POC template created: /playbooks/poc-privatedeploy-egress-checklist (internal).

maria (AE): Thanks all — super helpful. I'll reply to the customer by EOD with the checklist and pricing ballpark. :thumbsup:
